# Sizing run — 110 kg rider, standing attack position

Everything that rolls: **402 kg**, net CoM **0.45 m** above the pivot (drives hanging below the pivot act as part-counterweight)

## Roll — outer gimbal axis
- Inertia: 268 kg·m²; gravity moment at ±60°: 1549 N·m
- Peak demand (pulling up out of full lean at full accel): **3891 N·m**
- Sector tooth force: 16.2 kN shared by 2 pinions
- 100:1 → per motor 28.4 N·m incl. 1.25× margin + preload (5 kW peak 47.7) OK; 2500 rpm at 150°/s OK
- Runaway into the end stops at full speed: 920 J → buffers need 10° of travel at ≈5.3 kN·m (hard stops at ±63°, fully crushed at ±73°)
- Holding a 30° lean: 4.9 N·m per motor (rated 15.9) OK

## Pitch — inner gimbal axis
- Inertia: 269 kg·m²; gravity moment at +45° wheelie: 1510 N·m
- Peak demand: **3390 N·m** → per motor 25.0 N·m (5 kW) OK; 2000 rpm at 120°/s

## Yaw — continuous, slew ring + 2 pinions
- Inertia upright 109 kg·m², at 60° lean 300 kg·m²
- Peak demand: **1199 N·m** (incl. 150 N·m slew-ring drag)
- 80:1 → per motor 13.0 N·m (2 kW peak 19.1) OK; 2400 rpm at 180°/s

## Heave — along the stalk (the 'suspension')
- Carriage load 202 kg → static 1.98 kN; peak at 1.5 g onset **5.25 kN**
- 20 mm lead screw: peak 18.6 N·m (3 kW peak 28.6) OK; static 7.0 N·m, or 1.8 N·m with the air spring carrying 75 %
- 0.6 m/s → 1800 rpm; stroke 200 mm (±100)

## Structure
- Base/anchor design overturning moment (1.5 × peak axis torque): **5.8 kN·m**
- Stalk (114.3×8 CHS equivalent) bending at peak: 59 MPa → S355 safety factor 6.1

## Envelope (pivot 0.60 m above floor)
- Rider's head swings 1.67 m sideways at full lean; bar end 1.17 m
- Rear fender at full wheelie: 1.27 m behind the axis, 0.39 m off the floor
- Keep-out radius **2.0 m** → fenced cell ≈ 4.6 m × 4.6 m
- Minimum ceiling **3.0 m**; seat height above floor ≈ 1.55 m

## Why there's no overhead fall-arrest line
- A ceiling tether to the rider's chest pays out at **3.6 m/s** during an ordinary 150°/s whip. Self-retracting lifelines lock at ≈1.5 m/s, so one would yank the rider mid-whip.
